targetAudience.primary: Architects, security engineers and governance leads operating enterprise multi-agent systems
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands roles, delegated credentials, tool calls and policy enforcement.
targetAudience.readerProblem: Individually permitted calls can combine into a harmful outcome while every agent appears locally compliant.

whyNow: A primary preprint reports an Agentic Principal Chain mechanism over 3,154 evaluation instances, including strong blocking for policy-covered exfiltration cases alongside utility cost and residual uncovered harm.

externalHook.description: A read call and a send call may each be allowed while their composition exfiltrates data.

coreProposition: Delegated multi-agent authority should be enforced as a stateful authorization program: scope narrows across principal hops, budgets and prior actions accumulate, and composition closure is checked atomically before effects.

originalValue.description: Reframes delegated authority from per-agent permissions into infrastructure-held session state with monotone narrowing and composition closure.

readerTakeaway: Bind every delegated call to an ordered principal chain, narrowed scope, cumulative budget and prior-action state; serialize the admission update before effectful execution.

supported: The source reports a signed principal-chain session envelope and six conjunctive admission checks.
Covered exfiltration cases were strongly blocked in the reported benchmark.
Removing a required composition pair produced a reported 39.9% data-stealing rate and interactive enforcement incurred utility cost.
unsupported: Safety when the enforcement gateway is compromised
Automatic discovery of every harmful action composition

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument concerns general delegated authorization architecture.

decisionReason: The source exposes a concrete stateful mechanism, measurable tradeoffs and failure under incomplete composition policy.
